sounds.intro: Japanese has five pure vowels and very even rhythm. Every syllable gets the same time, with no heavy stress.
rows: oo, short and relaxed, lips not rounded
long o: hold it twice as long
long u: hold it twice as long
between "r", "l" and "d": a quick tap of the tongue
softer than English f, blow between both lips
hard g, as in "go" (many speakers soften it in the middle of words)
a tiny pause before it, like saying "hot-tea"
at the end of a word or before consonants: a hum "n"

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Japanese often drops pronouns. Use names instead of "you". The word "anata" (you) can sound too direct.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Japanese nouns do not change for singular or plural. "Hon" can mean one book or many books. Use a number and a counter to be exact.

grammar.title: Desu: to be
text: Japanese puts the verb last. "X wa Y desu" means X is Y. Wa (written ha) marks the topic.
ex: 私は医者じゃありません

grammar.title: Verbs: polite forms
text: Polite verbs end in -masu. Change it to -masen (not), -mashita (did), -masen deshita (did not).
ex: コーヒーを飲みません

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: Verb last. Order: topic (wa), place or time, object (o), verb. Say the topic first and the verb at the very end.
ex: I read a book at home
I will go to Tokyo tomorrow

grammar.title: Negation
text: Polite: -masen. Desu becomes ja arimasen. I-adjectives: -kunai desu. Past: -masen deshita.
Always shown with the positive form next to it.
ex: 彼女はここにいません
I do not have a car
私たちは疲れています
私たちは疲れていません
彼は日曜日に働きます
he does not work on Sundays
彼は日曜日に働きません

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Add ka at the end of the sentence. No word order change, and no question mark is needed.

grammar.title: Particles
text: Small words after nouns show their job. They are the glue of Japanese.
rows: subject; also with suki and wakaru
at / by (where or how you do it)

grammar.title: This, that, which
ex: sono hon wa watashi no desu
dore ga anata no desu ka
どれがあなたのですか

grammar.title: Adjectives
text: There are two kinds. I-adjectives end in -i (takai). Na-adjectives need "na" before a noun (kirei na hana). To make an i-adjective negative, change -i to -kunai.

grammar.title: Wanting and asking
text: Add -tai to the verb stem to say "want to". Add -te kudasai to ask politely.
ex: I want to go to Japan
ここで待ってください
ゆっくり話してください

grammar.title: Existing and having
text: Imasu is for living things, arimasu for things. To say "I have", say "[thing] ga arimasu".
ex: ここに銀行があります

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: Polite: desu / masu. Casual (plain): da, and the dictionary form of verbs (taberu, iku). Casual is only for friends and family.

grammar.title: Commands
text: Ask politely with the te-form plus kudasai. Say "please do not" with -naide kudasai. Plain commands are rude.
ex: ここに来ないでください
ドアを開けてください
watashi no hanashi o kiite kudasai
私の話を聞いてください
心配しないでください
ゆっくりお願いします
ちょっと待ってください

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: Can: verb stem + emasu, or koto ga dekimasu. Must: -nakereba narimasen. Want to: -tai desu. Must not: -te wa ikemasen.
ex: 手伝ってもらえますか
行かなければなりません
I do not want to eat
来ることができません
彼女は勉強したいです
今日働かなければなりません

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Ni = at or in (where something is). De = where you do something. Japanese puts the place word after the noun: "table no ue" = on the table.
ex: the book is on the table
hon wa tsukue no ue ni arimasu
本は机の上にあります
the cat is under the table
neko wa tsukue no shita ni imasu
the shop is next to the bank
mise wa ginkou no tonari ni arimasu
店は銀行の隣にあります
the park is near the station
kouen wa eki no chikaku ni arimasu
公園は駅の近くにあります
the key is in the bag
kagi wa kaban no naka ni arimasu
鍵はかばんの中にあります

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: "A wa B yori ..." means A is more ... than B. Use "ichiban" for "the most". Adjectives do not change for comparison.
ex: 大きい、もっと大きい、一番大きい
小さい、もっと小さい、一番小さい
kore wa are yori ii desu
これはあれよりいいです
kore wa are yori warui desu
これはあれより悪いです
kanojo wa watashi yori se ga takai desu
彼女は私より背が高いです
tashukento wa samarukando yori ookii desu
タシケントはサマルカンドより大きいです
